# Flow { #timetoalign.timelines.Flow }

```python
timelines.Flow(
    sections=list(),
    mode=FlowMode.default,
    folded_length=0,
    id='',
    source_metadata=dict(),
    _controller_ref=None,
)
```

A computed flow (sequence of measure visitations).

A Flow represents one possible path through a score, accounting for
repeats, jumps, and voltas. It can be:
- Computed by ScoreFlowController from MeasureData
- Loaded from .flow.csv ground truth
- Compared using is_equivalent()

Flows are section-based, using `sections` (list of PlaythroughSection)
for .flow.csv serialization and is_equivalent() comparison.

Flows computed by ScoreFlowController have a controller reference, allowing
access to MeasureUnits via iter_units(). Flows loaded from CSV are
"detached" and do not have controller access.

## Note {.doc-section .doc-section-note}

MC ranges use the **right-open interval convention** [mc_start, mc_end),
consistent with partitura and the TTA manuscript.

## Attributes {.doc-section .doc-section-attributes}

| Name            | Type                                                                                             | Description                                        |
|-----------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| sections        | [list](`list`)\[[PlaythroughSection](`timetoalign.timelines.flow.sections.PlaythroughSection`)\] | The sequence of PlaythroughSection objects.        |
| mode            | [FlowMode](`timetoalign.core.enums.FlowMode`)                                                    | The FlowMode used to compute this flow.            |
| folded_length   | [int](`int`)                                                                                     | Number of unique MCs (measures in printed score).  |
| id              | [str](`str`)                                                                                     | Identifier for this flow (defaults to mode.value). |
| source_metadata | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\]                                              | Optional metadata from the source MeasureData.     |

## Methods

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [diagram](#timetoalign.timelines.Flow.diagram) | Show playthrough section sequence for this flow. |
| [diff_diagram](#timetoalign.timelines.Flow.diff_diagram) | Show side-by-side comparison of this flow with another. |
| [diff_flows](#timetoalign.timelines.Flow.diff_flows) | Show differences between this flow and another using sequence alignment. |
| [from_csv](#timetoalign.timelines.Flow.from_csv) | Load Flow for specific mode from .flow.csv file. |
| [from_dataframe](#timetoalign.timelines.Flow.from_dataframe) | Create Flow from DataFrame with mc_start, mc_end, atomic_sections fields. |
| [from_records](#timetoalign.timelines.Flow.from_records) | Create Flow from list of dicts with mc_start, mc_end, atomic_sections. |
| [from_sections](#timetoalign.timelines.Flow.from_sections) | Create a Flow from PlaythroughSections. |
| [is_equivalent](#timetoalign.timelines.Flow.is_equivalent) | Compare by zipped (mc_start, mc_end) ranges. |
| [iter_units](#timetoalign.timelines.Flow.iter_units) | Iterate over MeasureUnits via the controller. |
| [to_atomic_sequence](#timetoalign.timelines.Flow.to_atomic_sequence) | Return flattened sequence of atomic section IDs. |
| [to_csv_rows](#timetoalign.timelines.Flow.to_csv_rows) | Export as .flow.csv format rows. |
| [to_dataframe](#timetoalign.timelines.Flow.to_dataframe) | Convert to pandas DataFrame with section information. |
| [to_mc_sequence](#timetoalign.timelines.Flow.to_mc_sequence) | Return the sequence of MCs in traversal order. |
| [to_records](#timetoalign.timelines.Flow.to_records) | Export as list of dicts (section-based). |

### diagram { #timetoalign.timelines.Flow.diagram }

```python
timelines.Flow.diagram(
    width=70,
    unicode=True,
    show_mcs=False,
    show_reasons=True,
)
```

Show playthrough section sequence for this flow.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name         | Type           | Description                                              | Default   |
|--------------|----------------|----------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| width        | [int](`int`)   | Total width of the diagram in characters.                | `70`      |
| unicode      | [bool](`bool`) | Use Unicode characters (True) or ASCII fallback (False). | `True`    |
| show_mcs     | [bool](`bool`) | Whether to expand MC sequences per section.              | `False`   |
| show_reasons | [bool](`bool`) | Whether to annotate why each section starts.             | `True`    |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type        | Description                                                           |
|--------|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | \'Diagram\' | Diagram object (displays as ASCII in terminal, rich HTML in Jupyter). |

### diff_flows { #timetoalign.timelines.Flow.diff_flows }

```python
timelines.Flow.diff_flows(other)
```

Show differences between this flow and another using sequence alignment.

Uses difflib to produce a human-readable diff of atomic sequences.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type     | Description                      | Default    |
|--------|----------|----------------------------------|------------|
| other  | \'Flow\' | Another Flow to compare against. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type         | Description                                              |
|--------|--------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [str](`str`) | String showing the alignment/diff between the two flows. |

### from_csv { #timetoalign.timelines.Flow.from_csv }

```python
timelines.Flow.from_csv(path, mode)
```

Load Flow for specific mode from .flow.csv file.

Filters CSV to rows matching the given flow_mode.

#### Note {.doc-section .doc-section-note}

MC ranges use right-open interval convention [mc_start, mc_end).

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type                                          | Description                 | Default    |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------|-----------------------------|------------|
| path   | \'Path \| str\'                               | Path to the .flow.csv file. | _required_ |
| mode   | [FlowMode](`timetoalign.core.enums.FlowMode`) | The FlowMode to load.       | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type     | Description                                |
|--------|----------|--------------------------------------------|
|        | \'Flow\' | New Flow instance with sections populated. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                             |
|--------|----------------------------|-----------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If no entries found for the given mode. |

### from_records { #timetoalign.timelines.Flow.from_records }

```python
timelines.Flow.from_records(records, mode)
```

Create Flow from list of dicts with mc_start, mc_end, atomic_sections.

#### Note {.doc-section .doc-section-note}

| Name    | Type                                          | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Default    |
|---------|-----------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| records | [list](`list`)\[[dict](`dict`)\]              | List of dicts, each with keys: - mc_start: int (inclusive) - mc_end: int (exclusive, right-open) - atomic_sections: str (semicolon-separated, e.g., "A;B");   the persisted flow-CSV format names this column   "atomic_segments", which is accepted as a fallback key | _required_ |
| mode    | [FlowMode](`timetoalign.core.enums.FlowMode`) | The FlowMode for this flow.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type     | Description                                |
|--------|----------|--------------------------------------------|
|        | \'Flow\' | New Flow instance with sections populated. |

### is_equivalent { #timetoalign.timelines.Flow.is_equivalent }

```python
timelines.Flow.is_equivalent(other)
```

Compare by zipped (mc_start, mc_end) ranges.

Two flows are equivalent if they have the same number of sections
and each corresponding section has matching mc_start and mc_end.

Note: atomic_section_ids are NOT compared - only MC ranges matter.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type     | Description                      | Default    |
|--------|----------|----------------------------------|------------|
| other  | \'Flow\' | Another Flow to compare against. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type           | Description                                    |
|--------|----------------|------------------------------------------------|
|        | [bool](`bool`) | True if flows are equivalent, False otherwise. |

### iter_units { #timetoalign.timelines.Flow.iter_units }

```python
timelines.Flow.iter_units()
```

Iterate over MeasureUnits via the controller.

This provides access to the folded score skeleton (one MeasureUnit
per MeasureData row).

#### Yields {.doc-section .doc-section-yields}

| Name   | Type                                                             | Description                      |
|--------|------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------|
|        | [MeasureUnit](`timetoalign.timelines.flow.measures.MeasureUnit`) | MeasureUnit objects in MC order. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                  |
|--------|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If Flow is detached from controller (e.g., loaded from CSV). |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> flow = controller.compute_flow()
>>> for unit in flow.iter_units():
...     print(f"MC {unit.mc}: next={unit.next}")
```

### to_atomic_sequence { #timetoalign.timelines.Flow.to_atomic_sequence }

```python
timelines.Flow.to_atomic_sequence()
```

Return flattened sequence of atomic section IDs.

This provides a canonical representation of the flow as a sequence
of atomic section traversals. Useful for comparing flows and debugging.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                           | Description                                    |
|--------|--------------------------------|------------------------------------------------|
|        | [list](`list`)\[[str](`str`)\] | List of atomic section IDs in traversal order. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> flow = Flow.from_sections([
...     PlaythroughSection(1, 17, ("A", "B")),
...     PlaythroughSection(17, 32, ("C",)),
...     PlaythroughSection(6, 17, ("B",)),
... ], FlowMode.default)
>>> flow.to_atomic_sequence()
['A', 'B', 'C', 'B']
```
